haiku-low.q1: A pull request builds the image and runs unit tests only, pushing and deploying nothing. A merge to main starts a release run, which can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Both deploy one image tagged with the commit SHA, built once on merge to main and pushed to the registry. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure gets one automatic retry and fails the run only if both attempts fail. Unit test failure ends the run immediately, with no retry.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs rollback: deploy.sh rollback staging restores the image in SSM previous_tag and sets current_tag to it. The run then ends as failed.
haiku-low.q5: Any member of release-approvers except the commit author can approve. If no valid approval comes within 72 hours, the run expires, production gets nothing, and Slack #deploys is notified.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store, per environment: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps its old image, canary is scaled to 0, and SSM tags are unchanged. Migrations stay applied, so the stable image must work with the new schema.
haiku-low.q8: It is superseded: at the production lock check, if production already runs a newer commit, it stops quietly with no deploy and no announcement.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it releases the lock and waits for Monday 09:00 UTC. For a concurrent deploy, one run holds the production lock at a time; queuing is not stated.
haiku-low.q10: Prometheus canary 5xx ratio and request count over the last minute, read by the run every 30 seconds for 15 minutes. A usable sample above 1% aborts; three unusable samples in a row also abort.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The document says the approval job records who approved and when, but not how approvers are notified or what information they receive.
haiku-low.q12: Staging is not rolled back automatically; the run ends and the environment stays as the script left it. Production redeploys the current_tag read at run start, not rollback, because previous_tag is an older version.

sonnet.q1: A PR builds the image (not pushed) and runs unit tests only; nothing deployed. A merge to main starts a release run, which is what can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image, tagged with the commit SHA, built once at merge. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration failure: retried once automatically; the run fails only if both attempts fail. Unit failure: no retry, run fails. Either way the run ends (the other suite is stopped if still running), failure announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q4: Run `deploy.sh rollback staging`, which sets the stable image back to the recorded SSM previous_tag (written by the successful staging deploy, so known-good). Then the run fails and is announced; if rollback itself fails, a human is paged.
sonnet.q5: A member of the release-approvers group who is not the commit author (author approvals are not counted). If no valid approval in 72 hours, the run expires, nothing goes to production, staging keeps the tag, and it is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag, per environment. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment unchanged. SSM tags unchanged (canary is never recorded). Database schema keeps any migrations the canary applied, since migrations are never undone. The canary is scaled to 0 via canary-off; the run fails and is announced (a human is paged if canary-off fails).
sonnet.q8: NOT STATED as an automatic cancel; the older run keeps waiting for approval. When it later reaches production, the superseded check (current_tag not an ancestor of its SHA) fails and it ends quietly without deploying or announcing. If still within 72 hours without approval it would expire.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it releases the production lock and waits (no lock, no time limit) for the next window, then reacquires the lock and rechecks. While another production deploy is in progress: it waits to acquire the production lock, since only one run can hold it. Superseded check can still end it.
sonnet.q10: Canary 5xx ratio (Prometheus query over last 1 minute) and its request count. The pipeline run reads them every 30 s for 15 minutes. Failure: a usable sample (at least 100 requests) with ratio above 1%, or 3 unusable samples in a row; also canary deploy failing or not ready in 300 s. Failure scales the canary to 0 and fails the run.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document only says CI approval jobs record who approved and when; it does not say how approvers are notified or what information they see.
sonnet.q12: Staging: deploy.sh rollback staging, restoring previous_tag, safe because a successful staging deploy already wrote both tags. But that is only after smoke test failure; a failed `deploy.sh staging` rollout itself is not rolled back automatically. Production: if deploy.sh production fails, run deploy.sh production <current_tag read at run start>, then canary-off, not rollback, because previous_tag is only written after success and holds an older version than current_tag. Failed stable rollouts in staging are left as the script left them (open question).
